starting_conditions.defense: Tarawa-derived lagoon-side fires, local reserves, registered mortar/artillery lanes, distributed ammunition/water and protected local communications survive in fragments after repeated bombardment.
starting_conditions.armor: No traced Japanese combat tank platoon.
starting_conditions.US: 7th Infantry Division with LVT/LVT(A), artillery from flanking islets, old-battleship/cruiser/DD gunfire, CVE support and medium/light tank packages. One LST-class hull was mission-killed on 5-Feb, reducing reserve/unloading margin without deleting an untraced cargo unit.

landing_cycle.result: First waves land successfully but encounter more immediate lagoon-side direct fire and pre-registered mortar fire than a surprised historical-equivalent defense. LVT(A), destroyer direct fire and supporting artillery suppress firing points quickly enough to prevent a beach denial event.
landing_cycle.traffic: Additional LVT/LST/engineer reserve creates intermittent beach-exit and wave-control congestion. Local 20-40 minute delays occur at specific exits; commanders meter later waves rather than feeding the queue blindly.

landing_cycle.result: US infantry expands a sustainable western beachhead while engineers clear exits and tanks begin systematic strongpoint reduction. Japanese local reserves counterattack or reoccupy positions in small packets rather than a mass daylight charge.
landing_cycle.geometry: US penetration is centered around 1.5-2.0 km from the western landing area in the more successful axes by evening, with bypassed positions and local dead ground preventing a clean straight front.

landing_cycle.result: Beachhead remains secure. Japanese defenders shift to infiltration, mortar fires and bounded local attacks against road/artillery/command nodes; a larger 6/7-Feb night effort is not yet fully resolved at T24.

US_vehicle_state.note: These are D-Day working loss/temporary-out bands across the southern assault system, not cargo lost on the 5-Feb LST hit.

Japan_T24.command: Local command cells and registered fires remain useful in pockets; island-wide coordination is too fragmented for a coherent beachhead-ejection attack.

assessment: This is the sector where the new fortification/sensor/C2 audit most visibly raises D-Day friction. The gain is time and local casualties, not strategic denial: flat terrain, lack of armor/depth and US division-scale tanks/engineers/gunfire remain decisive.
